title: Casper and the Hymn
premise: Lior Galloway takes a night-caretaker teaching post at Hollowmere School, where a class vanished decades ago and the surviving records hum with an unfinished hymn. The school's old sleep-study tapes begin answering his questions in a child's voice, revealing that the missing students were sung into the building's walls by a teacher who wanted justice the law refused to give. As Lior uncovers that he was the one child who escaped, his memory surgically erased, he must learn the hymn's final verse—the verse of release—without joining the chorus himself. In the end, Lior sings the last verse alone, freeing the children and unmaking his false identity, choosing to remember everything even as the school, and the man he pretended to be, dissolve around him.
about_author: Bram Marchetti is the pen name of a former boarding-school music instructor who left teaching after finding rehearsal recordings no one had made. Casper and the Hymn is their second novel, written mostly at night with the doors counted.

chapters.title: The Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Lior arrives at Hollowmere, a rural school with too few students and too many locked rooms, and learns the caretaking rules: keep the lights on, count the doors, never play the piano in Hall B. Told from Lior's POV, the chapter builds quiet unease as he notices chalk dust falling in an empty classroom. Emotional beat: wary belonging—he wants to be invisible here.

chapters.title: Sleep Study
chapters.summary: Lior discovers a cabinet of reel-to-reel sleep recordings from a 1970s study and plays one out of curiosity. Beneath a sleeping boy's breathing, a second voice answers questions no one asked aloud. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into dread as the voice says his name—a name he hasn't told anyone.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Digging through archives, Lior finds a class photo dated 1974 with faces scratched out and a teacher, Miss Vesper, circled. A retired janitor tells him about the 'missing class' and warns him the hymn they rehearsed was never finished. POV: Lior, with the janitor's testimony. Emotional beat: the thrill of investigation shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Lior sets up his own recorder overnight; the tape captures children singing two verses of a hymn, then stopping, waiting. When he asks who wrote the third verse, every light in the wing dies at once. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: terror mixed with a terrible recognition—the melody feels like something he once knew.

chapters.title: What the Walls Keep
chapters.summary: Following cold spots and counting doors that won't stay counted, Lior finds names carved inside a wall cavity: eleven children, all accounted for as 'transferred.' He realizes the transfers were lies. POV: Lior interwoven with fragments of a child's diary. Emotional beat: righteous anger—someone did this deliberately.

chapters.title: Miss Vesper's Reason
chapters.summary: Through letters hidden in the piano bench, Lior learns Miss Vesper discovered a benefactor abusing the children; when authorities buried it, she used an old folk rite—a sung binding—to hide the children somewhere justice could reach them. POV: Lior reading Vesper's letters. Emotional beat: horrified sympathy; her justice became a prison.

chapters.title: The Verse That Waits
chapters.summary: The children's voices grow urgent, singing nightly closer to Lior's room, and he begins humming harmonies he never learned. His reflection lags half a second behind him. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: identity unraveling—he is being remembered into the song.

chapters.title: Casper
chapters.summary: The voice on the tapes finally speaks plainly: 'You're Casper. You ran.' Lior's fabricated memories fracture—he was the twelfth child, the one who escaped the rite, his past excised and rebuilt. POV: Lior/Casper. Emotional beat: devastating self-recognition; staying invisible was always the wound.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: In Hall B, before the assembled dark, Lior must sing the final verse—release, not binding—without letting the song claim him as its twelfth voice. Miss Vesper's presence begs him to stop; the children pull him forward. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: climax of courage and sacrifice, singing alone against a chorus.

chapters.title: Doors, Uncounted
chapters.summary: Dawn finds the school empty, the wall cavity holding only chalk dust and eleven small shoes returned. Lior—no longer Casper, no longer quite Galloway—walks out without counting the doors, carrying every memory he paid to recover. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: mournful peace; justice outside the law, memory chosen over safety.
